method: Valgrind 3.22.0 DHAT, separate sequential processes running persistent_range_workload in release mode; all callback-count assertions passed

baseline.repeat: Second DHAT process produced identical totals and peak; Memcheck with the same binary and --test-threads=1 also reported 799 allocations and 222350 allocated bytes
baseline.harness_control: Removing --test-threads=1 yielded 803 allocations and 224056 allocated bytes, so the harness-thread setting alone does not explain the historical 1201 count

conclusion: Candidate peak live heap is approximately 3.15 times this baseline for the measured workload; resource costs remain unresolved.
limitations: DHAT peak live heap excludes thread stacks, allocator overhead and other mapped memory; it is not whole-process peak RSS.

The baseline allocation count differs from the historical 1201 count. Its cause is not established; retain historical observations separately and do not silently substitute them into this paired comparison.
Shared host with an unrelated local build gate running; no runtime comparison is inferred from these instrumented executions.
These profiles do not classify retained allocations as harmless or establish a general retention bound.
